audit_notes: Slip length: reported hydrodynamic slip on hydrogels and hydrated polymer brushes is 10-100 nm (e.g. Bocquet & Charlaix review; soft-gel claims of microns are not reproduced under controlled conditions); 200 nm is optimistic. Adjusted effective_slip_length 2e-7 -> 1e-7 m. b+ = 1e-7/5.4e-6 = 0.019 -> expected gain 0.1/95.1 = 0.1%, i.e. no meaningful drag reduction against a clean FR hull; ridge spacing 0.3 um = 0.06 viscous units -> hydraulically smooth (k+ << 1), no roughness penalty. Any real benefit of this concept is fouling resistance (hydration barrier against protein/ diatom adhesion), which the flow model cannot capture. Structural/durability: 1 um zwitterionic hydrogel swollen in seawater has modulus ~10-100 kPa; abrasion under cleaning and sand is the main failure mode; anchoring in the 0.3 um ridges improves adhesion but the ridge tips are exposed. Osmotic swelling in seawater (0.6 M) is smaller than in fresh water for zwitterions (anti-polyelectrolyte effect), which is favourable. Baseline: smooth FR wall with zero slip.

performance_gain.label: Skin-friction reduction vs clean FR hull
